ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The primary governing statutes are the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) for corporate formation, ownership and register maintenance, and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018 (as amended), together with the Financial Intelligence Unit Regulations 2019 and the AML/CFT Guidance Notes issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). UBO record-keeping and disclosure obligations are further developed through the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2021.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and authorised signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC SDN List, the UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the Samoa FIU internal watchlist. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs) in accordance with FATF Recommendations 12, 22 and 24, including source of funds and source of wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The Samoa FIU requires submission of a suspicious transaction report within 48 hours of suspicion and prohibits tipping-off.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Online International Companies Registry (managed by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, International Companies Registration Section)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or in the Samoan language. If a name is in Samoan, a certified English transliteration or translation must accompany the filing. The name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet, and must end with a limited-liability suffix such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', or the Samoan term 'Fa'asala' (if acceptable to the Registrar). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must not contain words implying government or public authority without prior approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed company name, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 working days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must specify the grounds of objection, include a certified copy of the proposed name search, and set out why the name satisfies the Act. The Registrar must issue a determination in writing within 21 working days. If the appeal is refused, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 28 days of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is not acceptable. The International Companies Act 1987 requires every international company to maintain a registered office in Samoa at a physical street address in Apia. The registered agent must verify the physical premises and may not use a post-office box or virtual workspace as the registered office. The Registrar will reject any filing that fails to provide a verifiable physical location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate (12% annual probability for the herbal wholesale and dried botanicals category). Unannounced physical inspections, however, are triggered when the designated registered agent is placed on an increased compliance watchlist or when there is a prior deficiency in UBO reporting. Because the stated business is bulk import/export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, which is classified as low-risk under Samoa's AML/CFT risk matrix, a physical inspection is most likely to occur during the incorporation year as part of a random compliance sample.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987-88 (Samoa), as amended — provisions governing incorporation by registration, execution of the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the appointment of a registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa, and the powers of an International Company; read together with the International Financial Services Act 2016 (Samoa)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies — Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Memorandum may fix authorized capital, commonly USD 10,000, and shares may be issued at par or for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account or capital deposit is required under the International Companies Act 1987-88.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, as filed with the Registrar of International Companies, be and are hereby allotted the initial subscribed shares set forth in the Register of Members, the agreed subscription consideration having been duly satisfied; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that such agent be authorized to accept service of process; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [DIRECTOR] be appointed as sole first director, [SECRETARY] as first secretary, and that the director be authorized to issue share certificates, open bank accounts, and execute documents necessary to carry out the Company's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), acting through a licensed registered agent in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent in Apia and submit the prescribed name reservation request identifying at least two alternative company names. The agent lodges the request with the Registrar of International Companies for a word-for-word availability search against the Register of International Companies and reserved-name records.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form (SIFA prescribed form)
Registered agent engagement letter
Identity documentation of the proposed subscriber/shareholder
Two or more proposed company names in rank order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused as undesirable, misleading, or identical to an existing entry, the registered agent refiles with substitute names; objections may be cured by adding a distinguishing numeral or geographical qualifier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association under the International Companies Act 1987-88, including objects broad enough to cover international wholesale of dried lycium (goji) botanicals and herbal products. The subscriber signs the instrument before a notary public or the registered agent, and the signature and date are witnessed in accordance with the Act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft and execution copies)
Subscriber consent and signature pages
Notarized identity documentation of the subscriber
Confirmation of authorized share capital structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar later queries the instrument, amend it by special resolution or supplementary memorandum; re-execution and re-notarization are performed before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, the registered agent's consent to act, confirmation of the registered office in Apia, and the statutory filing fee. The Registrar reviews the filing and, upon approval, issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent consent to act
Certificate of name approval
Government filing fee remittance
Registered office confirmation in Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is requisitioned, file an amended document within the period directed by the Registrar; minor objections are cured by a letter of clarification, and material defects require re-execution of the affected clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolutions and share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors of the newly incorporated International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold and minute the first board meeting by written resolution: allot shares to subscribers, formally adopt the registered office, appoint the first director and company secretary, authorize the opening of bank accounts, and issue share certificates to members.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting or written resolutions
Register of members and share certificates
Consent to act of directors and secretary
Registered office adoption instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective appointments are remedied by a subsequent written resolution re-appointing the same or substitute officers; share register corrections are made under a board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration statutory particulars and banking onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and licensed commercial banks in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File particulars of first directors, the secretary, and the registered agent with SIFA; then complete the corporate bank account application in the name of the International Company with Swift TT and wire transfer facilities, including beneficial ownership declarations and AML/KYC due diligence documents.
required_dossiers: Notice of directors and secretary particulars
Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Board resolution opening the bank account
AML/KYC forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking documentation is queried, supplement with apostilled corporate documents, updated registers, or a consolidating board resolution; if SIFA issues a compliance requisition, respond with verified particulars and refile as directed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (MAF) — Quarantine Division, jointly with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Trade and Commerce Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Export Plant Product Registration and Phytosanitary Certificate for Dried Lycium (Goji) and Herbal Botanicals

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Division of Environment and Conservation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) registration; full EIA not triggered for low-impact repacking, cleaning, and dry storage operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluent for dry repacking; where washing or cleaning is performed, wastewater must meet Samoa national effluent thresholds (BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0); no significant VOC emissions expected from low-temperature drying; solid botanical waste to be composted or disposed at a licensed facility

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); storage racking and structural load inspection under the MNRE building code; occupational health and workplace safety inspection by the MCIL Labour Division with no unresolved nonconformities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) – Government of Samoa; official e-services portal: sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) must obtain a Samoa Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) by submitting an application to the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) via the online registration facility or in person at the SRA Revenue Centre. The application must include the certificate of incorporation, the International Company's registered agent details, certified copy of the charter or articles of association, director and shareholder particulars, and the anticipated date of first taxable activity. Where the IC does not derive income sourced in Samoa and engages exclusively in offshore export trade, the TIN is issued for customs and VAGST compliance purposes only; the International Companies Act 2009 provides no requirement to obtain a domestic business license. Registration for VAGST is mandatory if taxable supplies exceed SAT 100,000 in any 12-month period; however, a tax-exempt IC whose supplies are exclusively exported is still required to hold a TIN to effect customs procedures and to claim zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election exists under Samoa tax law. An International Company is statutorily classified as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 2009 and the Income Tax Act 2020, and is not subject to Samoa income tax on foreign-source income or on transactions conducted through a licensed IC. The IC may elect to register as a domestic company by surrendering its International Company status, which triggers ordinary Samoa entity-level taxation. Hybrid mismatch elections under the Income Tax Act 2020 are only relevant to domestic corporate groups and are not applicable to International Companies outside the domestic tax net.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) – Samoa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 100,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; non-resident persons carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa are also liable to register if threshold is met
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently operate a real-time e-invoicing or mandatory fiscal clearance system. VAGST invoices are standard paper or electronic invoices specifying the supplier's TIN, invoice date, description, quantity, unit price, VAT amount, and total. Export clearances are processed through the Samoa Customs computer system (Asycuda World) via approved customs brokers; there is no API-based digital stamping requirement. Taxpayers with an annual turnover above the registration threshold must file VAGST returns electronically through the SRA e-services portal, but no transaction-level clearance or State-approved invoice stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods qualifies for zero-rating under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2009 where the supplier has sold the goods in the course of a taxable activity and the goods are either (i) exported by the supplier to a destination outside Samoa, or (ii) transported to an overseas principal, or (iii) removed from Samoa under customs control as provided under section 30A. For the International Company exporting dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, the following conditions must be met: a written export sales contract with a non-resident buyer, payment in a foreign currency from outside Samoa, physical departure of the goods from Samoa within 21 days after the invoice date or within a longer period approved by customs, and strict compliance with Samoa phytosanitary export licensing for plant-based commodities. Offshore services ancillary to the export (such as packaging and shipping) are zero-rated only if supplied directly to the overseas buyer of the goods; any services supplied to a Samoa resident remain subject to 15% VAGST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (CUSEXP) submitted in Asycuda World
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment out of Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims or export documentation misstatements may expose the International Company to a VAGST shortfall penalty equal to 150% of the tax avoided, together with interest accrual from the original filing date. The Samoa Revenue Authority may also issue an amended assessment and immediate clawback of any VAGST refund improperly claimed. Deliberate falsification of customs declarations triggers penalties under the Customs Act 2014, including fines not exceeding 300 penalty units and imprisonment for up to seven years; directors and officers involved in export invoice fraud are jointly and severally liable. Continuing failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline may be treated as deemed taxable income derived in Samoa, subjecting the IC to income tax at 27% on the unremitted amount, plus late payment penalties and collection action.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS / Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) — Exchange Control Division and Financial Institutions Supervision Department; statutory regulators under the Exchange Control Act 1976, Financial Institutions Act 1996, Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, and KYC/AML Rules 2008.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed-float currency subject to exchange control. Current account payments (trade, services, income) are generally authorized through licensed commercial banks acting as authorized dealers upon documentary verification. Capital account transactions — inbound equity subscription, shareholder loans, outward profit remittance, and cross-border lending — require prior CBS approval or notification unless expressly exempted. International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 are statutorily exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976 in respect of all non-resident, foreign-currency offshore transactions, meaning the WS_IC may freely receive equity, repatriate profits via dividends, and hold foreign currency accounts without CBS permits, provided no Resident of Samoa counter-party and no WST settlement is involved. Profit remittance from any residual WST onshore account remains approval-gated and requires audited financial statements, tax clearance from the Ministry of Revenue, and evidence of the underlying non-resident shareholding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must repatriate proceeds to an authorized dealer within 90 days of bill of lading date and surrender to WST unless a Foreign Currency Account is pre-approved; 100% conversion is the statutory norm for resident export receipts. The WS_IC (non-resident, exchange-control-exempt) is not subject to mandatory surrender, provided: (1) invoice is payable in USD/HKD/SGD to a designated offshore account; (2) CBS-approved bank receives the related shipping/contract dossier; and (3) no portion of proceeds is settled in WST or credited to a resident account. Any incidental onshore credit must be converted immediately and flagged for CBS quarterly reporting by the bank as a non-resident transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency USD/WST) — primary operating + capital escrow sub-ledger
Operational Trade Account + Foreign Currency Settlement Account (BSP network USD/AUD rails)
Operational Account (WST/USD) — acceptable secondary clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low-to-Medium. Samoa has no dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) licensing regime; offshore fintech banking platforms (Wise-style, Airwallex, Mercury, Currenxie) generally decline Samoa-IC structures because the jurisdiction is not on their supported coverage, FATF mutual evaluation improvements notwithstanding. Legal constraint: foreign EMIs may lawfully onboard the IC as a non-resident client without Samoan licensing only if the EMI's home regulator permits cross-border Pacific clients; the IC may use such EMIs solely as supplementary settlement conduits, never as the primary correspondent rail, because EMIs cannot issue SWIFT MT103 directly and create an unregulated bridge that bank compliance teams will treat as a red flag.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical/face-to-face verification is the de facto mandate for all three tier-1 banks: the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and at least one director must attend an interview at the Samoa branch or at an ANZ/BSP branch anywhere in the Pacific or Australia via the bank's internal network with the file reviewed by the Samoa compliance team. Remote video KYC is not accepted in practice. Exception: where travel is impossible, banks accept a notarized statutory declaration sworn before a Samoa-licensed lawyer (or foreign notary with apostille), the original certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, full register of directors/shareholders, board resolutions authorizing account opening, and a corporate structure diagram naming all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trust/nominee ownership structure obscuring true beneficial ownership — the classic Samoa IC red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the trust deed or nominee declaration; signed UBO declaration form (AML form prescribed by CBS); corporate ownership chart; annotated articles evidencing appended bearer-share prohibition; original share register and transfer ledger; professional reference letter from the registered agent (Samoa International Finance Authority licensed).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume dried goji berry procurement from PRC/Hong Kong with traceability gaps and sanctioned-party screening conflicts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreement with final beneficial owners of each supplier; quarantine/phytosanitary certificates; USDA/European import inspection documentation; bill of lading and warehouse receipts; payment schedule tying each MT103 to a specific commercial invoice; entity-level sanctions/PEPS screening output for the whole counterparty chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual incoming capital injection sourced from third-party non-shareholders or pooled family funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; certified source-of-funds dossier (audited financial statements of the remitter, bank statements covering 12 months, evidence of wealth origin); board resolution approving the specific transaction; tax identification numbers of all funding parties; confirmation that the injection is booked to the capital/loan escalation account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business scope (ISIC 4631 wholesale of dried fruit/herbs) and account activity (escrow cycles, rapid in-and-out clearing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying trade contract for each cycle; escrow facility agreement; pre-shipment inspection certificates; pipeline-forecast dashboard presented to the bank monthly; certification that flows are 100% physically settled with no unbacked pass-through; audited trial balance evidence matching receivables and inventory physically in transit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity/loan: SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or UBO account with purpose code 'EQUI' (Share Capital Contribution) or 'INTY' (Intercompany Loan), beneficiary being 'WS_IC — Capital Escrow Account' at ANZ/BSP Samoa. Pre-funding compliance pack: executed board resolution authorizing issuance of shares; capital subscription ledger; certified copies of remitter identification and sanctions clearance; and a written confirmation that the injection is a non-resident foreign-currency transaction exempt from CBS approval. Banks will quarantine the credit for 1-3 business days pending matching against the signature card and source-of-funds dossier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements use: (1) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer to Hong Kong/Singapore/PRC beneficiary banks for goji berry containers; (2) Irrevocable Documentary Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 issued by ANZ/BSP Samoa for high-value herbal bulk purchases (60-90 day usance); (3) Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for repeat low-risk vendors. Every outbound transfer requires underlying copy of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and purchase order to satisfy the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 obligations; WST-denominated outbound flows trigger CBS approval and potential 1-week delay, so USD/HKD settlement accounts are mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (up to 12-24 months) — permitted only with authorized dealer banks on evidence of an underlying trade exposure; margin requirement 5-15%

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD executed offshore in Singapore or Hong Kong — permitted for the IC as a non-resident; cash-settled, no Samoa regulatory approval required, hedge ratio capped at documented purchase-order exposure

Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed-to-floating USD/HKD/USD/WST) — permissible only when paired with the shareholder loan or trade-payable matching notional; CBS approval required if a Samoan resident counterparty is involved; prohibited for speculative purposes
Purchased FX Options (premium-only, long position on the currency pair) — permitted; writing/selling options is not permissible for a corporate non-bank without an FX dealer license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and annual government renewal fee (International Companies Act 1987, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa (submitted by licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the exact anniversary date of incorporation; no fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late penalty of 10% of the overdue annual fee; administrative strike-off risk after 3 months in arrears; Registrar-ordered dissolution after 6 months with reinstatement only upon full payment of arrears, penalties, and restoration application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) confirmation statement and UBO Register verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (submitted through licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Co-terminous with the annual renewal cycle, within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of beneficial ownership rules is a statutory offence carrying monetary penalties and personal officer liability; persistent non-compliance triggers the same administrative strike-off procedure as unpaid annual fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: On-site Statutory Register audit and annual sign-off (Register of Members, Directors, Charges, Minutes, UBO Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulatory filing; register audit conducted by the licensed registered agent and certified true copy maintained in the company records in Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Conducted at each anniversary date, promptly after the Annual Return is submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers at the registered office is an offence; officers are liable to fines and the International Company may be refused certificates of good standing, with eventual strike-off for continued default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a tax-exempt non-resident International Company; audit becomes mandatory only for ICs licensed as banks, insurers, trustees, or fund administrators, or where the company's constitutional documents require an audit, or where the Registrar directs an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as applicable in Samoa; for dormant non-resident international companies, record-keeping sufficient under section 174 of the International Companies Act to show transactions, assets, and liabilities is accepted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each anniversary the registered agent issues a UBO confirmation statement; every director and shareholder must confirm or update the beneficial owner schedule within 30 days. Any share transfer or indirect ownership change during the year must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days and recorded in the UBO Register before the next Annual Return is lodged.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – 1,200 per annum (licensed registered agent and registered office, excluding government renewal fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – 4,000 per engagement (certified audit/review, incurred only when required by financiers, buyers, or voluntary appointment)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a qualifying International Company (IC) on all income derived outside Samoa, pursuant to section 177 of the International Companies Act 1987, as amended; ordinary resident companies are otherwise taxed at a headline rate of 25% under the Income Tax Act 2015.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The IC enjoys a complete statutory exemption from Samoa income tax, capital gains tax, gift duty, inheritance duty, stamp duty on instruments executed in respect of IC business, and exchange control restrictions. No corporate income tax return is required. The only annual costs are the IC government licence fee (scaled to authorised capital), registered office/agent fees, and an economic substance declaration fee where applicable. There is no payroll tax for offshore employees and no deemed distribution tax on exempt IC income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFSA Registrar of International Companies - Annual Licence Renewal and Economic Substance Declaration (submitted exclusively through a Samoa-licensed registered agent; the IC does not file an income tax return with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue because it is a tax-exempt entity).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual government licence fee must accompany the declaration. A grace period is not statutorily granted, though the Registrar routinely allows a further 30 days before penalty accrual.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the registered name matches the articles of association and all banking records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIFSA/ROC registration number assigned at incorporation (format: IC-XXXXX).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refer to the registered agent's compliance ledger; any discrepancy must be rectified before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total authorised share capital and class of shares; the annual licence fee is determined by the capital band.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare in the original currency of incorporation (commonly USD or WST); undervaluation triggers penalty and strike-off risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Concise description of the commercial activity for the reporting year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For this entity: 'International wholesale and bulk export of dried goji berries (Lycium barbarum) and mixed herbal botanicals (ISIC 4631); no domestic Samoa sales.'

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Registered Office and Agent Confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming the registered office in Samoa maintained by a licensed international company agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A local physical registered office is mandatory; a mere mailing address is insufficient for IC good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that a register of beneficial owners is maintained at the registered office as required by the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners must be identified by name, nationality, residential address, and a 100% ownership chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of whether the IC conducts a 'relevant activity' and, if so, the substance indicators satisfied within Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wholesale distribution and export trading is a relevant activity; the IC must evidence local management, employees, premises, and operating expenditure in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual fee amount remitted by the registered agent to the Samoa Ministry of Finance via SIFSA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must advance funds to the agent before the anniversary date; non-payment produces immediate penalty accrual.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of the annual licence fee attracts a penalty of 10% of the unpaid fee, with an additional 10% penalty for each further year or part-year of default. The Registrar may strike the IC off the register after three months of arrears, and restoration requires payment of all outstanding fees, a restoration fee of WST 1,000, and a fresh annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Ministry of Revenue - Nil Income Tax Return (not applicable to a compliant tax-exempt IC; provided here only as the fallback position if the IC loses its exempt status).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: If the IC were to be assessed as an ordinary Samoa-resident company, the income year would end on 31 December and the return would be due on the following 30 June.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Samoa-source and foreign-source business activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC may claim the section 177 exemption only if it has not conducted domestic Samoa trade and has filed the annual substance declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business deductions under the Income Tax Act 2015.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Original invoices supporting goji berry procurement and logistics must be retained for seven years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% corporate income tax on chargeable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply for an exemption determination before the due date; retrospective claims are not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an income tax return where a return is in law required attracts a penalty of 20% of the assessed tax, plus monthly interest of 2%, under the Tax Administration Act 2015.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory final withholding tax on dividends is 15% for dividends paid by a Samoa-resident ordinary company (Income Tax Act 2015). Dividends distributed by a tax-exempt International Company out of income derived outside Samoa are not subject to Samoan withholding tax, provided the IC has maintained its exempt status and holds no Samoa-sourced income. Treaty-reduced rates of 5% on direct holdings of 10% or more and 15% otherwise apply under the Samoa-Australia, Samoa-New Zealand, and Samoa-China double taxation agreements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate from the Ministry of Revenue. Application protocol: (1) written application on Form TRC-01 executed by a duly authorised director or the licensed agent; (2) certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; (3) certificate of good standing from SIFSA; (4) declaration of central management and control located in Samoa, including minutes of board meetings held in Samoa; (5) declaration of beneficial ownership; (6) payment of the WST 150 processing fee; (7) issuance usually within 15 business days. The TRC must accompany the source-country tax authority forms (e.g., Australian ATO Form TD1 or the relevant treaty relief form). Treaty relief will be denied if the IC is a pure conduit with no economic substance in Samoa or if the applicable DTA limitation-of-benefits clause excludes tax-exempt residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan withholding tax is 15% for interest, 15% for royalties, 15% for management fees, and 15% for technical service fees paid to non-residents. Under Samoa's principal DTAs, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties to 5% or 10% depending on the treaty partner. A compliant International Company paying royalty or interest to a foreign lender in respect of offshore business is protected by the IC tax exemption, but the IC must nonetheless document the payment with a withholding declaration and the lender's tax residency certificate to avoid a deemed withholding assessment under section 118 of the Income Tax Act 2015.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No specific monetary threshold in WST is prescribed by statute for Local File or Master File preparation under the Income Tax Act 2015 or Tax Administration Act 2015. The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may issue a notice requiring transfer pricing documentation for any cross-border transaction with a related party, regardless of amount. Prudent compliance practice is to maintain a functional analysis, a benchmarking study, and a local transfer pricing file where annual related-party turnover with non-residents exceeds WST 2,500,000, or where the aggregate book value of related-party intercompany balances exceeds WST 10,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2021 and associated Rules apply economic substance requirements to International Companies conducting relevant activities. Wholesale distribution and export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals constitutes a distribution and service centre relevant activity. The IC must satisfy: (i) conduct core income-generating activities in Samoa, including contract negotiation, procurement decisions, inventory risk management, and invoicing; (ii) direct and manage the business in Samoa through board meetings held in Samoa; (iii) maintain adequate physical premises in Samoa; (iv) employ a number of staff proportionate to the trading activity; and (v) incur local operating expenditure proportionate to the level of profits booked in Samoa. An annual economic substance declaration must be filed with the Registrar through the licensed agent, and underlying records must be retained for six years. Failure to meet the substance test results in financial penalties, deregistration, and reporting to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately mischaracterising goji berry export revenue as a non-taxable loan, booking offshore sales through undisclosed related-party conduits, destroying or falsifying invoices, contemporaneous contracts, or shipping records, or making a false statement in the annual economic substance declaration to preserve the IC tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 2015, civil shortfall penalty of 100% of the avoided tax plus monthly interest of 2%, regardless of the IC's nominal exempt status; criminal conviction for tax evasion carries a fine of up to WST 20,000 and imprisonment for up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the tax shortfall on grounds of dishonest assistance; the court may issue a travel ban and order surrender of passports; proof of fraudulent evasion extends the imprisonment term to five years and disqualifies the individual from serving as an officer of a Samoa international company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining nominal Samoa registration while the wholesale goji berry business is entirely managed, staffed, and controlled from Hong Kong, mainland China, or another foreign jurisdiction, with no board minutes in Samoa, no local employees, no local office, and no local expenditure, yet continuing to rely on the IC tax exemption and treaty network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with the International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2021 attracts a penalty of WST 250,000 to WST 500,000; the Registrar may strike the IC off the register, seize the annual fee guarantee, and notify the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, resulting in adverse cross-border tax transparency reports and possible blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false substance declarations are personally liable for the regulatory penalty and for costs of the Registrar's investigation; upon strike-off, courts will pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally accountable for unsatisfied third-party trade creditors of the herbal wholesale business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain a complete and current register of beneficial owners; knowingly or negligently accepting Swift TT and wire transfer settlement proceeds from third parties linked to sanctions evasion, drug trafficking, or illicit herbal supply chains; or structuring payments below reporting thresholds to avoid scrutiny by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017, a corporate fine of up to WST 50,000 applies for register breaches; the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 imposes fines of up to WST 300,000 and imprisonment for up to 14 years for laundering, and the FIU may issue freezing orders over bank accounts held by the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who act with willful blindness to the source of funds are treated as accessories to money laundering and face personal fines of WST 50,000 and 14 years' imprisonment; the court may prohibit departure from Samoa, compel disclosure of foreign bank accounts, and order confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Activity and Breach of IC Perimeter
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting wholesale sales of dried goji berries to persons resident in Samoa or maintaining a fixed place of domestic business without a Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998, or exporting herbal botanicals without the required sanitary and phytosanitary export licence from the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries / Ministry of Health.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the IC perimeter under section 181 of the International Companies Act 1987 invalidates the tax exemption and subjects the IC to ordinary corporate income tax; the Business Licences Act 1998 imposes a fine of WST 10,000 plus a continuing daily penalty of WST 100; unlicensed herbal export results in product forfeiture and a health regulatory fine of up to WST 5,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for all unpaid corporate fines and enforcement costs; the Registrar may revoke the IC's certificate of incorporation and the licensed agent's registration; courts may disregard the corporate entity and order personal restitution of profits derived from the illegal domestic trading activity.
